fixes.explanation: That's the order, friend. The Lord says, "Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake. Topple them on the heads of all the people…" (Amos 9:1) I think this is one of those moments where you just hold your breath and keep reading.

Ha! If only it were a polish job. I'd bring my own rag. But the Lord says, "Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake." (Amos 9:1) Nothing gets shined here. The order is to strike the tops of the pillars.

Yep, the serpent. The Lord says, "…there I will command the serpent to bite them." (Amos 9:3) Look where that line lands: "though they hide from Me at the bottom of the sea." Even down there, He says they won't be hiding from Him.

Melts, yes. The text says the Lord GOD of Hosts is the One "…who touches the earth and it melts, and all its dwellers mourn…" (Amos 9:5) One touch, and the earth melts. I think that's a good moment to just sit with how big He is.

This one is true, friend. The text says, "He summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth." (Amos 9:6) That's the Lord GOD of Hosts doing the summoning. Then the verse closes with "The LORD is His name."

Yes, not even a pebble. The LORD says He will shake Israel like grain in a sieve, "but not a pebble will reach the ground." (Amos 9:9) Not one pebble hits the ground. I once lost a whole sprinkle jar down a drain and I'm still not over it.

I see why you'd say that, since shaking a sieve sounds like things falling. But the LORD says He will shake Israel like grain in a sieve, "but not a pebble will reach the ground." (Amos 9:9) None hit the ground, friend, not even one.
